$ rhythm-roadie explain uncovered-column
# uncovered-column: a column that looks personal has no rule (medium)

What: A text column no profile or columns: rule covers, whose name looks
personal (email, phone, name, address, ip, dob and similar) or whose sampled
values are 20% or more emails or phones.

Why it matters: Roadie only rewrites what a rule covers. An unknown table with
customer data would reach the copy as it is.

What Roadie does: copy and prepare stop before writing anything (exit 1,
error code uncovered) unless --allow-uncovered; plan lists each column.

By hand: Add the column under columns: in .roadie/config.yaml with its rule,
e.g. table: wp_loyalty_members, column: email, rule: email. rhythm-roadie
config init --from <source> suggests the entries.


$ rhythm-roadie explain key.stripe-live
# key.stripe-live: a live Stripe secret or restricted key (critical)

What: A live Stripe secret or restricted key in the database, wp-config.php,
.env or, for a site target, in code.

Why it matters: A live key lets the copy act as production at the provider:
charge cards, send mail or messages, change accounts.

What Roadie does: swap (the default) replaces it with the test key set under
keys.test_keys when that key is a test key, else blanks it; blank blanks every
live key. A key in code is reported with action manual: Roadie only edits the
database, wp-config.php and .env.

By hand: Give a test key in keys.test_keys (for example ${ROADIE_STRIPE_TEST})
or blank the value, then run verify.


$ rhythm-roadie explain target-is-production
# target-is-production: the target is production (exit 3)

What: The target's URL host, siteurl, home, SSH host or database host matches
production:.

Why it matters: Roadie never writes to production; there is no override.

By hand: Point --to at the staging copy.


$ rhythm-roadie explain pseudonymised
# pseudonymised: what Roadie's copies are

Pseudonymised data is still personal data under the GDPR (Article 4(5), Recital 26).
This report shows what Roadie's checks found in this copy; it is not a statement that
the copy holds no personal data. Signed by roadie:7Q3kXc2… (rhythm-roadie report check report.json):
the signature shows who ran Roadie, which version and rules, on which input and that
the report is unchanged since. It doesn't prove the data holds no personal data.
